subject: Ephemeral routing & TTL: clarifying data eviction and 'no-derivative' modeling assurances
messages:
From: Security Team <security@acmecloud.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Legal <legal@acmecloud.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on ephemeral routing, TTL and guarantees on not training models

Mina — thanks for taking this call yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our security team after reviewing the whitepaper: we need written confirmation on two points before legal signs off: 

1) "No-derivative/model training" assurance — does Redwood persist any customer request/response data in a way that could be used for future model training, even transiently (snapshots, logs, debug copies)? If there are temporary artifacts, what is the maximum TTL and who has access?

2) Ephemeral routing & TTL — we heard about prefix caching and routing fallbacks. Can you provide the eviction policy for KV/prefix caches and any overlap where customer tokens could be present on shared GPUs or transient storage?

If you can provide a short statement and any supporting docs (matrix of retention windows by artifact type) that would be ideal. We may need a short redline to the standard DPA.

Thanks,
Nikki Shah
Security Program Manager – Acme Cloud
security@acmecloud.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Security Team <security@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on ephemeral routing, TTL and guarantees on not training models

Hi Nikki — appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front, followed by a brief breakdown (I appended a link to our internal playbook for deeper details).

- Short assurance: Redwood does not train or improve models using customer request/response data for hosted or dedicated customers unless an explicit opt-in for "derivative learning" is signed. We can provide contractual language for the DPA.

- Transient artifacts: we maintain several ephemeral artifacts (request logs, serving telemetry, per-request KV cache entries) to support routing, debugging, and autoscaling. These are short-lived and governed by TTLs. Under default hosted settings, the maximum TTL for any transient artifact that could contain customer prompt text is 72 hours; most operational caches are < 6 hours.

- Access: access to ephemeral artifacts is strictly role-based and audited. Only SRE/ops on-call and a small set of troubleshooting engineers can access logs, and access requests are logged. Customer-designated private deployments (VPC/on-prem) do not surface those artifacts to Redwood-managed SREs by default.

Details (high level):
* KV/prefix cache: per-tenant entries are kept in memory or in encrypted local SSD on the node; eviction policy is LRU with TTL per-entry. For hosted tiers TTL defaults to 2 hours and max-configurable TTL is 72 hours with customer consent.
* Snapshots & backups: full snapshots are taken for debugging in rare failure cases and are encrypted; snapshot retention for debug snapshots is 30 days but snapshots that contain customer payloads are redacted or tombstoned within 72 hours unless customer approves extended retention.
* Telemetry/metrics: aggregate-only by default; any raw request sampling used for debugging is redacted and treated as ephemeral.

I'll attach the retention matrix and our playbook link. If you want, Marissa can coordinate a short note for the DPA redline.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Ben — forwarding Acme's security questions. Can you confirm the implementation details below, especially around:

- Max-configurable TTL for per-tenant KV/prefix cache (we say 72h max in the response)
- Where snapshots may land (encrypted local SSD vs S3) and timeline to tombstone any customer payloads
- Whether there is any scenario where artifacts land in a model training queue or persist into our model ops pipelines without explicit opt-in

Thanks — please reply all with short bullet confirmations, so I can forward to the customer.

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Jul 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on ephemeral routing, TTL and guarantees on not training models

Mina/Marissa — quick confirmations below for Acme: 

- KV/prefix cache TTL: default 2h; tenant-level config up to 72h with signed consent. Eviction LRU; persisted only in node-local encrypted RAM/SSD. No writes to long-term object storage unless explicitly captured for debugging.

- Snapshots & debug dumps: on rare incidents we create encrypted diagnostic snapshots. These are staged on an internal encrypted object store and are subject to a strict retention workflow: auto-redact/tombstone job runs at 72h to remove customer payloads; full snapshot deletion at 30 days unless flagged and approved by the customer for extended retention.

- Training pipelines: there is no automated path that pulls production request/response artifacts into our model training pipelines. Model training datasets are curated from separately consented data sources. Any human review or sampling for model improvement requires an explicit opt-in and is tracked via a consent ledger.

- Access & audit: access is RBAC + time-limited elevation; all reads of ephemeral artifacts are logged and subject to security review.

I'm attaching the retention matrix PDF we share with security reviewers. Happy to join a short call if Acme wants to walk through an architecture diagram.

Regards,
Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
